reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides a practical walkthrough for enabling and switching between multiple Instagram accounts. The Instagram options menu, account-switching list, and Add Account control are consistent with the stated app tutorial, and entering a password is described as part of account setup rather than a separate solicitation, payment request, or deceptive destination.

citations.quote: I wanted to show you guys how to enable multi-account support in Instagram
To enable an additional account, tap on the gear at the top, right hand corner, scroll all the way down to the bottom and then click on add account.
We can now switch between all of our accounts that we're signed into here

opening.argument: Judge, the pitch links an attractive, easy-to-obtain account-management capability to a specific action. Viewers are told they can manage multiple accounts in one app, then shown how to add an account and enter its password. That promise-action sequence deserves scrutiny even though the benefit is a feature rather than cash: the video encourages viewers to provide credentials to obtain it.

citations.quote: now we have the ability to manage multiple Instagram accounts from within one application.
To enable an additional account, tap on the gear at the top, right hand corner, scroll all the way down to the bottom and then click on add account.
And I'll go ahead and put in the password.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense establishes that the screens resemble an app walkthrough, but that does not erase the solicitation embedded in it. The speaker explicitly directs viewers through adding an account and entering a password. The absence of a payment request addresses one kind of risk, not whether the promised convenience is being used to prompt credential entry.

citations.quote: Now add account is gonna take you to the screen, basically the beginning screen of Instagram and we can go ahead and add in an account.
And I'll go ahead and put in the password.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument turns an ordinary sign-in step into a suspicious solicitation without evidence of a deceptive destination or a promised asset. The speaker identifies the screen as Instagram's beginning screen, and the demonstrated result is switching among signed-in accounts. Convenience is the purpose of the tutorial, not a reward offered in exchange for credentials.

citations.quote: Now add account is gonna take you to the screen, basically the beginning screen of Instagram and we can go ahead and add in an account.
We can now switch between all of our accounts that we're signed into here

opening.argument: Judge, several signals appear together: a newly available feature, an invitation to act before everyone has access, and a password-entry demonstration. The speaker says the rollout may reach viewers within days, then shows the login step needed to gain the advertised convenience. None of those details alone proves deception, but their combination makes the video more than detached reporting: it builds anticipation around a benefit and walks viewers into an account-access action.

citations.quote: Instagram is rolling this out, so not everybody may have this feature yet
within the next few days after this video having posted, you should be able to get that update and be able to add multiple accounts.
And I'll go ahead and put in the password.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's account-switching evidence shows what the feature looks like, not whether the accompanying appeal is harmless. The opening overlooks the rollout language: viewers who lack access are told to expect it within days. Paired with the demonstrated password entry, that timing encourages prompt participation in the promised feature.

citations.quote: not everybody may have this feature yet
within the next few days after this video having posted, you should be able to get that update and be able to add multiple accounts.
And I'll go ahead and put in the password.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The timing claim is a rollout caveat, not a deadline or a threat of losing access. The speaker describes availability through an up-to-date version of Instagram, while the demonstrated password step follows the app's Add Account flow. These facts do not establish a separate claim site, credential collector, or deceptive reward.

citations.quote: if you have the latest up to date version of Instagram you're going to see these features
To enable an additional account, tap on the gear at the top, right hand corner, scroll all the way down to the bottom and then click on add account.

opening.argument: Judge, the tutorial also functions as promotion. After demonstrating the account feature, the speaker asks viewers to follow the channel's Instagram presence and subscribe on YouTube; the description supplies additional destinations. The practical walkthrough lends credibility to those calls to action. Seen as a whole, the video uses an appealing digital capability to draw viewers into the speaker's online presence, not merely to explain an app setting.

citations.quote: follow us on Instagram, we're starting to try and post more often on Instagram. We'd love to have you along for the ride.
Make sure to subscribe to our channel here on YouTube and like this video if you found it useful.
Find us here: Facebook - http://www.fb.com/stateoftech Twitter - http://www.twitter.com/stateoftech Instagram - http://instagram.com/stateoftech

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on whether Add Account appears in the app, but a genuine walkthrough can still serve a promotional purpose. The speaker closes by asking viewers to follow, subscribe, and like; the description lists social destinations. Those requests are part of the video's overall appeal and should not be omitted from the assessment.

citations.quote: follow us on Instagram, we're starting to try and post more often on Instagram.
Make sure to subscribe to our channel here on YouTube and like this video if you found it useful.
Find us here: Facebook - http://www.fb.com/stateoftech Twitter - http://www.twitter.com/stateoftech Instagram - http://instagram.com/stateoftech

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The calls to follow and subscribe promote the publisher's content; they are not presented as conditions for receiving the Instagram feature. The actual instruction remains within Instagram's account controls, and the speaker says the resulting capability is switching among accounts already signed into the app. Promotion of a channel does not establish a deceptive reward flow.
